channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Forex Today: Focus shifts to Nonfarm Payrolls as Middle East tensions remain high
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Friday, June 5:

item.title: S&P 500: Tech wobble but breadth improves – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank analysts describe a mixed backdrop for US equities, with the S&P 500 rebounding on broad participation even as chipmakers lag after Broadcom’s disappointing AI guidance.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecasts: Pound returns abopve 215.00 amid broad-based Yen weakness
item.description: The Japanese Yen’s (JPY) mild recovery attempt seen during Friday’s Asian session has been short-lived.

item.title: Canada Unemployment Rate forecast to remain unchanged in May
item.description: Statistics Canada will release its Labour Force Survey on Friday, and markets are bracing for quite a steady print. The Unemployment Rate is expected to remain at 6.9% in May, while the Net Change in Employment is forecast to increase by 10K, reversing April’s 17.7K drop.

item.title: Oil: Prices stay subdued despite Hormuz risk – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior Market Strategist Benjamin Picton stresses that Oil markets remain in focus as Brent futures fell sharply even with the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed in their baseline.

item.title: Neither inflation nor the RBA: What's actually driving the Australian Dollar lower
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) is navigating rough waters, in the stark divergence between persistent domestic inflation and slowing economic growth.

item.title: Dow Jones futures edges lower due to cautious mood ahead of US Nonfarm Payrolls
item.description: Dow Jones futures inch lower 0.04% to near 51,650, while S&P 500 futures fall 0.64% to near 7,550. And Nasdaq 100 futures plunge 1.23%, trading near 30,110 during the European hours on Friday, ahead of the US regular opening.

item.title: US Dollar: Jobs data volatility fades fast – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister argues that a stronger United States (US) labour market only matters for the US Dollar (USD) if it shifts rate-hike expectations.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Jobs data and BoC doubts support upside versus USD – ING
item.description: Francesco Pesole at ING flags that weak April Canadian labour data and a still-dovish jobs contribution to Bank of Canada policy contrast with a widening USD/CAD two-year swap spread and emerging USMCA risk premium.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Pressure persists on 0.7120 support against USD – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight lingering downside momentum in AUD/USD after recent declines, with the pair hovering just above 0.7120 support. A clear break below 0.7120 could open the way toward 0.7095, while resistance is seen at 0.7150–0.7165.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecasts: Euro recovery stalls below 0.8655 in risk-off markets
item.description: The Euro (EUR) moves higher for the third consecutive day against the British Pound (GBP) on Friday, although bulls are failing to find acceptance above 0.8655.

item.title: British Pound faces second straight weekly loss as tensions in the Middle East weigh ahead of US NFP
item.description: The GBP/USD pair holds modest gains near 1.3420 during the European trading hours on Friday. Despite the intraday rebound, the pair is set to register its second straight weekly loss as tensions in the Middle East weigh.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD falls to near $72.50 as inflation risks prevail
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) depreciates after registering modest gains in the previous day, trading around $72.50 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Wednesday.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Trades subduedly near 1.3900 ahead of US-Canada employment data
item.description: The USD/CAD pair trades marginally lower at around 1.3900 during the European trading session on Friday. The Loonie pair is expected to trade with caution in the countdown to the United States (US)-Canada labor market data for May, which will be published at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Holds gains above 0.5850, but stays constrained under 100-day SMA
item.description: The NZD/USD pair trades with mild gains around 0.5865 during the early European session on Friday, bolstered by hawkish signals from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ). All eyes will be on the US Nonfarm Payrolls data for May, which is due later on Friday.

item.title: Nonfarm Payrolls set to show stable labor market in May as markets digest Fed hawkish shift
item.description: The United States (US) Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) will release the Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for May on Friday at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risks rise near 160 versus US Dollar – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research’s FX & Credit Strategist Chang Wei Liang notes that USD/JPY is trading close to 160, a level seen as a potential trigger for FX intervention.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Safe-haven appeal under pressure – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s FX Strategist Sim Moh Siong highlights a weaker Swiss Franc as EUR/CHF drifts higher from 0.91 support, reflecting widening rate disadvantages and the SNB’s active resistance to currency strength.

item.title: Japanese Yen edges up but remains close to the 160.00 intervention threshold
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) edges up against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, but the USD/JPY pair remains above 159.90 at the time of writing, unable to put a significant distance from the 160.00 level, considered the limit of tolerable JPY weakness for Japanese authorities.

item.title: Gold: Range trade persists on rates focus – ING
item.description: ING’s commodities team reports that Gold rebounded nearly 2%, briefly topping $4,500/oz, as a tentative Israel-Lebanon ceasefire reduced immediate geopolitical risk, before easing when Hezbollah rejected the deal.

item.title: US Dollar: NFP risks seen balanced – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan expects the upcoming US nonfarm payrolls release to show a moderate slowdown after April’s 115k gain, with consensus at 88k already reflecting soft expectations.

item.title: Turkish Lira: Sticky inflation and lira risks – Commerzbank
item.description: Ghose at Commerzbank expects Turkey’s May Consumer Price Index (CPI) to show only modest month-on-month moderation after April’s spike, keeping inflation momentum uncomfortably high.

item.title: Indian Rupee gains as RBI unveils measures to boost foreign inflows, leaves Repo Rate steady
item.description: The Indian Rupee gains against the US Dollar (USD) after Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) monetary policy decision; with the USD/INR pair sliding to near 95.35.

item.title: Euro: Downside risks toward key supports against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann see EUR/USD consolidating near 1.16 with momentum indicators flattening intraday, but the broader bias tilting lower.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Falls to near 0.7100 after slipping below 50-day EMA
item.description: AUD/USD depreciates after registering minor gains in the previous day, trading around 0.7120 during the Asian hours on Friday. The technical analysis of the daily chart shows the pair consolidating sideways within a rectangle pattern, as neither bulls nor bears gain control.

item.title: Gold slumps as lack of US‑Iran ceasefire progress weigh ahead US jobs data
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) attracts some sellers to near weekly low during the early European session on Friday. The precious metal remains volatile amid ongoing geopolitical turmoil.

item.title: Euro advances on rising ECB rate hike odds, US NFP eyed
item.description: EUR/USD extends gains for the second successive day, trading around 1.1620 during the Asian hours on Friday.

item.title: WTI flattens near $91 despite Israel-Lebanon fragile ceasefire
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, trades flat at around $91.00 during the early European trading session on Friday. The oil price consolidates even as the United States (US)-brokered ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon is proving to be fragile due to continued attacks between them.

item.title: AUD/JPY Price Forecast: Eases to near 114.00, but maintains bullish structure above 100-day SMA
item.description: The AUD/JPY cross loses traction to around 114.00 during the early European session on Friday. Fears of currency intervention from Japanese authorities provide some support to the Japanese Yen (JPY) against the Australian Dollar (AUD).

item.title: Swiss Franc gains despite fading SNB rate hike odds
item.description: USD/CHF remains subdued for the second successive day, trading around 0.7890 during the Asian hours on Friday. The Swiss Franc (CHF) strengthened despite softer-than-expected inflation data, which cooled market anticipation of an upcoming Swiss National Bank (SNB) rate hike.
